title: Correct metering for embeddings / rerank / function-call workloads on non-chat endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are observing incorrect billing and quota enforcement for a subset of non-chat endpoints that perform embeddings, reranking, and function/tool calls with structured outputs. Symptoms discovered from customer reports and internal spot-checks include: double-counting of token/embedding usage during rerank flows, tool-call arguments being billed as model tokens rather than as tool invocation metadata, and quotas/rate limits being applied at an incorrect scope for batched non-chat requests.

Root cause hypothesis (current assessment):
1) Metering pipeline tags requests by 'chat' vs 'non-chat' only; hybrid flows (e.g., rerank which internally computes embeddings) are not getting the 'embeddings' metering path, causing both embedding compute and rerank scoring to be billed incorrectly or duplicated downstream.
2) Function-calling/tooling layer serializes tool arguments into the same token stream that the token-metering job consumes, so tool-call metadata sometimes counts toward per-token quotas and per-token billing.
3) Rate limiter keying uses conversation_id / session for quota windows. Non-chat endpoints using request-level batching end up hitting the wrong quota bucket or are throttled unfairly (customers sending multi-request batches get aggregated under a single bucket).

Impact:
- Several enterprise customers and internal invoice reconciliation show billing mismatches (up to ~17% overcharge on certain rerank-heavy workloads).
- Quota/rate-limit enforcement has led to false throttles for high-throughput embedding pipelines.
- High potential for financial and SLA/customer-care escalations if not remediated.

Proposed corrective plan (breakdown):
A) Immediate mitigation (hotfix, 2 days):
- Add an attribute to the request envelope request_type = one of {text, chat, embedding, rerank, toolcall, structured-output} emitted at ingress (proxy layer) and carried through RPCs. This will allow meter to select the correct counting path deterministically.
- Patch token-meter to ignore tool-argument serialization when source_tag == 'toolcall' and instead increment a tool-call counter metric.
- Update rate limiter to prioritize request_id + endpoint_name for non-chat endpoints rather than conversation_id; deploy in feature-flagged mode.

B) Medium-term fix (1 sprint):
- Rework metering pipeline to adopt event-based primitive: emit discrete MeterEvent objects at the point of compute (embedding_compute, rerank_score, function_invoke, model_token_consumed). Each event includes request_type, model_variant, sequence_length, and cost_bucket so downstream billing can deduplicate and attribute correctly.
- Add integration tests that replay production trace samples from the billing-recon dataset and assert invariants (no double-count, per-request cost within +/-2%).

C) Backfill & reconciliation (1–2 weeks):
- Run reconciliation on historical windows flagged by analytics (last 60 days) to identify potential overcharges. Prepare a refund/credit plan in coordination with PM & Finance for affected customers.
- Add logging and dashboards for newly created MeterEvent types to validate correctness before mass reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests added and passing for embedding/rerank/toolcall metering paths.
- Rate limiter operates per-request for non-chat endpoints behind a feature flag and shows zero false-positive throttles on synthetic high-throughput replay.
- Billing pipeline emits distinct events for embedding_compute and rerank_score; end-to-end cost attribution for rerank flows matches ground truth traces within +/-2%.
- Finance & PM review sign-off on reconciliation plan and message cadence.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Emitting MeterEvent objects increases event volume and storage; we need a cost estimate vs. expected reduction in disputes. If too expensive, consider compact delta-format where events are aggregated per-request at the edge.
- Backfill reconciliation has legal/finance implications; seek early alignment with legal on thresholds for mandatory refunds.

Links / Evidence:
- Internal analytics dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.example.com/dashboards/metering/rerank-imbalance (requires SSO)
- Example overcharge customer case: INC-987 (PM notes)
- Reproduction trace sample (sanitized): https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/sanitized-meters/trace-20260111.json
